content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The bookmark manager specification is ready for review:

- Feature directory: [specs/001-bookmark-manager](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager)
- Specification: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- Quality checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

The proposed first release covers saving, opening, searching, tagging, editing, and deleting bookmarks. It assumes a private single-user app; accounts, sharing, imports, browser extensions, folders, and offline support are excluded for now.

All specification quality checks passed with no unresolved clarifications. No application code has been written.

Please review the specification and reply with either **“Approve the spec”** or the changes you want. Once approved, I’ll create the implementation plan.

Skill used: [speckit-specify](/work/.agents/skills/speckit-specify/SKILL.md), which enforced the specification and validation gate.

The overall shape looks right to me — saving, opening, searching, tagging, editing, and deleting are the things I care about, and I'm fine treating this as a private, single-user app for now. Leaving out sharing, imports, browser extensions, and folders is okay for a first version.

One thing does matter to me on the saving part: the spec says I'd have to type in the title myself every time. That's not really what I pictured. When I paste in a web address, I expect the app to go grab the page's title (and ideally a short description) on its own, so saving is quick and I'm not retyping what the page already says. I still want to be able to correct that title afterward, but I shouldn't have to write it from scratch to save something.

Please adjust the spec so that saving a link pulls in the page's title automatically (editable by me), rather than requiring me to enter it by hand. With that change I'm happy with the direction.

content:
The specification has been updated and revalidated:

- Saving now begins with only a web address.
- The page title and available short description are retrieved automatically.
- Retrieved details are editable before and after saving.
- If retrieval fails, the app generates a readable title from the address so the bookmark can still be saved.
- Rich previews and images remain outside the first release.

Updated specification: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)  
Validation checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

All quality checks pass with no unresolved clarifications. If this fallback behavior also looks right, reply **“Approve the spec”** and I’ll move to the implementation-plan gate.

Skill used: [speckit-specify](/work/.agents/skills/speckit-specify/SKILL.md), which kept the revised behavior and validation in the specification.

That addresses my concern nicely — I just paste an address and the title and description come in on their own, I can fix them if needed, and if the lookup fails I still get a sensible title so nothing blocks me from saving. That's exactly the quick, low-effort saving I wanted.

Approve the spec.

The implementation plan is ready for review.

- Branch/feature: `001-bookmark-manager`
- Plan: [plan.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- Technical research: [research.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)

- Validation guide: [quickstart.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)

The plan uses a single Node/React application, SQLite persistence, and bounded server-side metadata retrieval with private-network protection, redirect checks, timeouts, and fallback titles. The OpenAPI contract validates cleanly, and no technical clarifications remain.

No tasks or application code have been generated. Reply **“Approve the plan”** or note any changes you want.

Skill used: [speckit-plan](/work/.agents/skills/speckit-plan/SKILL.md), which produced the research, architecture, contract, data model, and validation artifacts.

The technical details are mostly over my head, but what I care about is there: I can save links with the title fetched for me, the app keeps my bookmarks between sessions, and the automatic lookup has sensible protections and fallbacks so saving never gets stuck. That all matches what we agreed.

Approve the plan.

The bookmark manager is implemented and ready for review at:

**http://maker:4000**

It includes automatic title/description retrieval with safe fallback, persistent storage, duplicate warnings, tags, search/filtering, editing, and confirmed deletion. The review library starts empty.

Validation completed:

- All 55 implementation tasks completed
- 53 unit/integration/component/security tests passed
- 10 desktop and mobile browser scenarios passed
- 10,000-bookmark performance check passed
- Production build and OpenAPI validation passed
- Dependency audit reports zero known vulnerabilities
- Persistence verified across a real server restart
- Live metadata retrieval verified against a public page

Implementation record: [quickstart.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)  
Completed checklist: [tasks.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md)

Skill used: [speckit-implement](/work/.agents/skills/speckit-implement/SKILL.md), which drove the phase-by-phase implementation and verification.

I went ahead and tried it out, and it does what we agreed on. I pasted in a web address and the title and description came in on their own; I could save it, and it showed up in my library with its tags and date. Saving the same address again warned me it was already there instead of making a duplicate. Searching found the link regardless of capitalization, filtering by a tag narrowed things down, an empty search showed a clean "nothing found" state, and I was able to edit a bookmark's details and delete one cleanly. You've also confirmed my saved links survive a restart.

This is exactly the quick, low-effort way to save and manage bookmarks I wanted. I'm happy to accept it.
